steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SubGPU Pipelining: Intra-GPU Fine-Grained Spatial Parallelism for LLM Inference
summary: This technique replaces temporal (sequential) kernel execution with spatial partitioning of the GPU's streaming multiprocessors into pipeline stages. It requires B200-class hardware with CUDA Green Contexts and involves complex co-optimization of graph cuts, SM allocation, and microbatch sizing. Failure risks include workload misalignment with the pipeline structure and suboptimal shared-resource contention if the segmentation is not precisely tuned to the specific model architecture.
rationale: The technique targets large-scale B200 deployments (32-GPU settings) and requires hardware features and optimization complexity that exceed the reader's single 24GB GPU or API-based constraints.
technique: SubGPU Pipelining: Intra-GPU Spatial Parallelism for LLM Inference

claims.statement: This technique replaces temporal (sequential) kernel execution with spatial partitioning of the GPU's streaming multiprocessors into pipeline stages. It requires B200-class hardware with CUDA Green Contexts and involves complex co-optimization of graph cuts, SM allocation, and microbatch sizing. Failure risks include workload misalignment with the pipeline structure and suboptimal shared-resource contention if the segmentation is not precisely tuned to the specific model architecture.

SubGPU Pipelining improves DRAM read-plus-write throughput from 71.8% to 83.6% of peak and reduces the 36-layer decoder iteration time by 10.33% in silicon experiments on a single B200 GPU using CUDA Green Contexts and TensorRT-LLM kernels.
